\paragraph{Exact source locations used here.}
The classification inputs are \cite[Chapter~VI, Theorem~1.1 and
Table~10, pp.~243--244]{BHPV2004E},
\cite[Theorems~4.2 and~5.1, with proofs, pp.~17--21 and~27--29]{OVV2020},
\cite[Theorem~1, p.~1]{BBK2019}, and
\cite[Theorem~2.1]{Catanese2004}.
The no-curve theorem is credited to Inoue by
\cite[Theorem~3.1, p.~303]{KhaledTeleman2026Journal}; the actual
unramified double cover is in its proof of Remark~3.5, p.~305.
The exceptional intersection identity is
\cite[\S I, p.~6]{Mumford1961}; the proof above supplies its
local analytic function and its exact exceptional-divisor map.
The current source records distinguish theorem-statement openings
from complete source-proof readings. The sign and equality assertions
are proved through the displayed normalization, conductor, filling
and intersection maps, with the stated irreducible-or-NC scope for
the global conclusion.

exact_owner_rows.outcome: proved as stated On a smooth rational normalization, torsion adjunction gives an actual anticanonical divisor. Its complete cubic and ruled minimal-model cases have the stated elliptic, cycle or simply connected rational-support topology. Under each allowed blowup the pole coefficient is multiplicity minus one; collapsing the inserted rational tree gives the explicit fundamental-group isomorphism. Every initially nontrivial reduced nodal case remains reduced nodal and gives the NC conclusion by P4.20. In the other cases both normalization and conductor are simply connected, so the conductor pushout identifies pi1(S) with the curve graph free group. Virtual abelianness bounds its rank by one and gives positive curve Euler number; the open-support bound completes the positive sign. Source proof and historical review records were available; this is a re-derivation, not a blind check.
